scenes.heading: JWT Authentication & Auth Middleware
scenes.narration: Let's learn stateless authentication in Go using JSON Web Tokens and a small auth middleware that guards your routes.

scenes.heading: Anatomy of a JWT
items: Three base64url parts: header, payload, signature
The payload is only encoded, not encrypted — anyone can read it
The signature proves integrity, not confidentiality
scenes.narration: A JWT is three base64url segments joined by dots: a header naming the algorithm, a payload of claims, and a signature over the first two parts. The key thing to internalize is that the payload is only encoded, never encrypted, so anyone can read it — never put secrets in it. The signature is the only thing proving the token wasn't tampered with and was minted by a key holder.

scenes.heading: The auth flow
steps: Verify the password once with bcrypt at login
Client sends it as a Bearer token
Middleware parses and validates the JWT
The subject is injected into the request context
scenes.narration: The flow starts at the front door: verify the password once with bcrypt, which is deliberately slow, then mint a short-lived signed token. The client sends that token on every request as a Bearer header. Your auth middleware parses and validates it — cheap, fast crypto with no database lookup — and on success injects the user into the request context so downstream handlers never re-parse the token.

scenes.heading: The security-critical keyfunc
scenes.narration: This keyfunc is where JWT security lives or dies. Before returning the key, it asserts the signing method is HMAC — that pin blocks the notorious alg-equals-none and algorithm-confusion attacks where an attacker dictates the algorithm. And notice we check both the error and token-dot-Valid: a token can parse structurally yet still be expired or invalid, so checking only the error would let expired tokens straight through.

scenes.text: Pin the algorithm, always check token.Valid, and use short access tokens plus refresh rotation since JWTs can't be revoked early.
scenes.narration: Always pin the algorithm in your keyfunc and always check token-dot-Valid. And because a signed JWT stays valid until it expires, use short-lived access tokens paired with rotating refresh tokens so a leaked token's damage is bounded.
